data.description:
Energy costs remain under pressure from Middle East conflict, and that keeps reliable baseload power in focus. Nuclear energy stocks sit at the intersection of this energy security story and the hunt for lower carbon power. For investors, that combination can be hard to ignore. Worley (ASX:WOR)

Overview: Worley is a global engineering and professional services company that supports energy, chemicals and resources projects, with a meaningful part of its low carbon energy work focused on nuclear power engineering, project delivery and lifecycle services from design to decommissioning. For investors interested in nuclear energy, Worley offers exposure through concrete, revenue generating nuclear contracts within a broader, diversified project portfolio.

Operations: Worley reports segment level revenues through adjustments and associate share totalling about A$11.1b, with geographic exposure spread across the Americas at A$6.2b, Europe, Middle East and Africa at A$4.0b, and Australia, Pacific, Asia and China at A$1.4b.

Market Cap: A$5.3b

Worley provides nuclear exposure through hands-on engineering and asset services for reactors and fuel cycle facilities, while also participating in wider energy transition and infrastructure spending. Forward-looking indicators such as earnings forecasts and valuation multiples are sometimes used by analysts to compare companies with peers, including for businesses with a mix of nuclear and sustainability-related work, as well as a long-term project backlog. Silex Systems (ASX:SLX)

Overview: Silex Systems is a technology commercialization company that develops and licenses its SILEX laser isotope enrichment technology, with its clearest nuclear link coming from uranium enrichment for nuclear fuel used in power reactors. It also has smaller activities in silicon and medical isotope enrichment and cREO semiconductor technology.

Operations: Silex Systems generates most of its A$13.3 million revenue from its Silex Systems segment, with a smaller A$2.1 million contribution from Translucent and an inter segment adjustment of A$1.7 million.

Market Cap: A$1.4b

Investors looking at nuclear fuel rather than just uranium mining may find Silex Systems interesting because its SILEX laser enrichment technology is aimed at the enrichment step of the fuel cycle, where value can be concentrated if licensing and commercial uptake progress. The company is still loss making, with a declining ROE and reliance on external borrowing, so a lot depends on whether uranium enrichment projects and Silex USA gain traction. At the same time, a long tenured management team, governance that appears reasonably balanced and current analyst forecasts of strong revenue growth together indicate a story that is still being written, and the most important chapters hinge on how the enrichment roll out actually unfolds.

Overview: Paladin Energy is an Australian uranium company that develops and explores uranium deposits in countries such as Namibia and Canada, producing uranium concentrate that feeds directly into the nuclear fuel supply chain for power reactors.

Operations: Paladin Energy currently generates its reported revenue of about $248 million entirely from Namibia.

Market Cap: A$4.8b

Paladin Energy provides direct exposure to uranium production at a time when nuclear power remains central to long term baseload and lower carbon electricity planning. The flagship Langer Heinrich mine is back in production and supported by a book of long term uranium contracts. The Patterson Lake South project in Canada adds a high grade growth option that is expected to see further drilling and updated resource work in 2026. The stock is still unprofitable and carries funding and execution risk, and the current valuation reflects expectations of a strong uranium cycle. Pinnacle West Capital (PNW) has scheduled a Special Call on 10 August 2026, drawing investor attention to potential updates regarding its Arizona-focused regulated electricity business and recent share performance.

See our latest analysis for Pinnacle West Capital.

The Special Call comes as Pinnacle West Capital’s share price has eased in recent weeks, with a 1-day share price return of a 2.03% decline and a 30-day share price return of an 8.41% decline, while longer term total shareholder returns of 10.71% over 1 year and 56.74% over 5 years indicate that momentum has built over time.

Most Popular Narrative: 7.3% Undervalued

The most followed narrative currently places Pinnacle West Capital's fair value at $105.07, above the last close of $97.36, which frames the recent pullback in a different light.

The ongoing influx of large commercial and industrial customers (notably data centers and manufacturers), along with a backlog of nearly 20 GW in uncommitted customer interconnection requests, signals substantial upside potential for volumetric sales and rate base expansion, positively impacting revenue and long-term earnings.

Investments in grid modernization and resiliency (such as advanced infrastructure for wildfire mitigation, automation, and predictive maintenance) position Pinnacle West to capitalize on increasing electrification and decarbonization efforts, supporting both operational efficiency and margin stability.
